subject: math
title: Money: Canadian Coins and Bills
seo_title: Grade 1 Money Worksheets: Canadian Coins and Bills with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Identify the various Canadian coins up to 50¢ and coins and bills up to $50, and compare their values
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on money for the Ontario curriculum: name the nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie, know the $5, $10, $20 and $50 bills, compare values, and count nickels and dimes to 50¢. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Look at the value, not the size of the coin.
key_sub: Nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢, loonie $1, toonie $2. The small dime is worth more than the big nickel. Count nickels by 5s and dimes by 10s.
body_html:
Canadian coins

Each coin has a name and a value. Size does not tell the value. The dime is the smallest coin, but it is worth more than the nickel.

CoinValueLook for
nickel5¢bigger than a dime
dime10¢the smallest coin
quarter25¢bigger than a nickel
loonie$1gold colour, 11 sides
toonie$2silver ring, gold centre

Canadian bills

Read the number on the bill. $50 is the most. $5 is the least.

Which is worth more?

Look at the value, not the size. 10¢ is more than 5¢, so a dime is worth more than a nickel.

Count by 5s and 10s

Count nickels by 5s. Count dimes by 10s. With both, start with the dimes.

Example

How much are 4 nickels?

Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢.

Answer: 20¢

Example

How much are a $20 bill and a $5 bill?

$20, then count on 5: $25.

Answer: $25

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The nickel is bigger, so it is worth moreLook at the value. The small dime is 10¢. The nickel is 5¢
4 nickels, so 4¢Count the value: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢
More coins is more money3 nickels (15¢) are less than 2 dimes (20¢)
A toonie is $1A loonie is $1. A toonie is $2

faq.q: What do Grade 1 students learn about money in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum (Financial Literacy, F1.1), Grade 1 students name Canadian coins up to 50¢ and coins and bills up to $50, and compare their values.

faq.q: Why does my child think a nickel is worth more than a dime?
faq.a: The nickel is bigger, so it looks like more. Put a dime and two nickels side by side and say “10¢ is the same as 5¢ and 5¢.” Size does not tell the value.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn Canadian coins at home?
faq.a: Use real coins. Sort them, say each name and value, then count nickels by 5s and dimes by 10s. Let your child pay for something small at the store.

faq.q: Do Grade 1 students learn about pennies?
faq.a: No. Canada stopped giving out pennies in 2013, so the nickel is the smallest value coin. Grade 1 uses the nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie.

items.e: This is a loonie. It is gold in colour. It is worth $1.

items.q: What is this coin called?

items.q: Which one is the nickel?
items.e: The nickel is worth 5¢. It is B. The dime is smaller, but it is 10¢.

items.q: Which one is the dime?
items.e: The dime is worth 10¢. It is C. It is the smallest coin.

items.q: Which one is the quarter?
items.e: The quarter is worth 25¢. It is A.

items.q: Which one is the loonie?
items.e: The loonie is worth $1. It has 11 sides. It is D.

items.q: Which one is the toonie?
items.e: The toonie is worth $2. It is D.

items.q: Which one is a bill?
items.e: The $10 bill is a bill. It is A. The toonie, quarter and loonie are coins.

items.q: Which coin has 11 sides?
items.e: The loonie has 11 sides. It is gold in colour.

items.q: Which coin has a gold centre?
items.e: The toonie has a silver ring and a gold centre. The loonie is all gold.

items.q: Which coin is the smallest?
items.e: The dime is the smallest coin. It is worth 10¢.

items.q: How many coins are there?
items.e: The quarter, the loonie and the dime are coins. That is 3 coins. The $5 and $20 are bills.

items.q: What is the name of the $1 coin?
items.e: The $1 coin is the loonie. The $2 coin is the toonie.

items.q: What is the name of the $2 coin?
items.e: The $2 coin is the toonie. “Two” and “toonie” sound alike.

items.q: What is the name of the 25¢ coin?
items.e: The 25¢ coin is the quarter.

items.q: What is the name of the 10¢ coin?
items.e: The 10¢ coin is the dime. The nickel is bigger, but it is only 5¢.

items.q: What is the name of the 5¢ coin?
items.e: The 5¢ coin is the nickel.

sets.title: What is each coin and bill worth?

items.q: How much is a nickel worth?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. It is bigger than a dime, but worth less.

items.q: How much is a dime worth?
items.e: A dime is worth 10¢. It is small, but it is worth more than a nickel.

items.q: How much is a quarter worth?
items.e: A quarter is worth 25¢, not 20¢.

items.q: How much is a loonie worth?
items.e: A loonie is worth $1. The toonie is $2.

items.q: How much is a toonie worth?
items.e: A toonie is worth $2. The loonie is $1.

items.q: Which coin is worth 5¢?
items.e: The nickel is worth 5¢. It is A.

items.q: Which coin is worth 10¢?
items.e: The dime is worth 10¢. It is D. Small, but worth more than a nickel.

items.q: Which coin is worth 25¢?
items.e: The quarter is worth 25¢. It is A.

items.q: Which coin is worth $1?
items.e: The loonie is worth $1. It is D.

items.q: Which coin is worth $2?
items.e: The toonie is worth $2. It is C.

items.q: Which bill is worth $20?
items.e: Read the number on the bill. The $20 bill is D.

items.q: Which bill is worth $50?
items.e: Read the number on the bill. The $50 bill is C.

items.q: How do we write the value of a dime?
items.e: A dime is ten cents. We write 10¢. $10 is ten dollars, much more.

items.q: How do we write five dollars?
items.e: Dollars use the $ sign in front: $5. 5¢ is five cents, much less.

items.q: How do we write the value of a quarter?
items.e: A quarter is twenty-five cents. Cents use the ¢ sign after the number: 25¢.

items.q: 2 nickels make the same as 1 ____.
items.e: 5¢ + 5¢ = 10¢. That is the same as 1 dime.

items.q: 2 loonies make the same as 1 ____.
items.e: $1 + $1 = $2. That is the same as 1 toonie.

items.q: How many nickels make 1 dime?
items.e: A nickel is 5¢. 5¢, 10¢. So 2 nickels make a dime.

items.q: The dime is small. How much is it worth?
items.e: Size does not tell the value. The small dime is worth 10¢. The bigger nickel is 5¢.

items.q: Which coin is worth 25¢?
items.e: The quarter is worth 25¢. The nickel is worth 5¢.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The nickel is 5¢. The dime is 10¢. So the dime is worth more. The nickel is bigger, but size does not tell the value.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The dime is 10¢. The quarter is 25¢. So the quarter is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The quarter is 25¢. The loonie is $1. So the loonie is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The loonie is $1. The toonie is $2. So the toonie is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The quarter is 25¢. The nickel is 5¢. So the nickel is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The loonie is $1. The dime is 10¢. So the dime is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The toonie is $2. The quarter is 25¢. So the quarter is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The toonie is $2. The $5 bill is $5. So the $5 bill is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The $5 bill is $5. The $10 bill is $10. So the $10 bill is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The $20 bill is $20. The $10 bill is $10. So the $20 bill is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The $50 bill is $50. The $20 bill is $20. So the $20 bill is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The $5 bill is $5. The loonie is $1. So the loonie is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth the most?
items.e: Loonie $1, quarter 25¢, dime 10¢, nickel 5¢. The loonie is worth the most.

items.q: Which is worth the least?
items.e: Toonie $2, quarter 25¢, dime 10¢, nickel 5¢. The nickel is worth the least.

items.q: Which is worth the most?
items.e: $50 bill $50, $20 bill $20, $10 bill $10, $5 bill $5. The $50 bill is worth the most.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 2 nickels: 10¢. 1 dime: 10¢. They are worth the same.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 3 dimes: 30¢. 1 quarter: 25¢. So the 3 dimes are worth more.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 1 quarter: 25¢. 4 nickels: 20¢. So the quarter is worth more. More coins or bills is not always more money.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 3 loonies: $3. 1 toonie: $2. So the 3 loonies are worth more.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 2 $20 bills: $40. 1 $50 bill: $50. So the $50 bill is worth more. More coins or bills is not always more money.

items.q: Count by 10s. How much money is this?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢. That is 20¢. 2¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 10¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: Count by 5s. How much money is this?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢. That is 10¢. 2¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 20¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢. That is 30¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 15¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: Leah finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢. That is 15¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 30¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢. That is 40¢. 4¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 20¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢, 50¢. That is 50¢. 5¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 25¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: Arjun finds these coins in his pocket. How much is it?

items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢, 35¢. That is 35¢. 7¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 70¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢, 35¢, 40¢. That is 40¢. 8¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 80¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: Owen has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢, 35¢, 40¢, 45¢, 50¢. That is 50¢. 10¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 100¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: 10¢, 15¢. That is 15¢. 2¢ counts the coins, not the cents.

items.q: Mateo finds these coins in his pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: 10¢, 15¢, 20¢. That is 20¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 25¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: Priya puts these coins in a piggy bank. How much is in it?
items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest first. Start with the biggest one. Count on: 10¢, 20¢, 25¢. That is 25¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 20¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 35¢. That is 35¢. 4¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 25¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest first. Start with the biggest one. Count on: 10¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢, 35¢. That is 35¢. 5¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 40¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest first. Start with the biggest one. Count on: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢, 45¢. That is 45¢. 5¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 30¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢).

items.q: Emma finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: 25¢, 30¢. That is 30¢. 2¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 35¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢). A quarter is 25¢, not 20¢.

items.e: Put the coins in order, biggest first. Start with the biggest one. Count on: 25¢, 30¢, 35¢, 40¢. That is 40¢. 4¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 55¢ mixes up the nickel (5¢) and the dime (10¢). A quarter is 25¢, not 20¢.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each $5 bill is $5. Count by 5s: $5, $10. That is $10. $2 counts the pieces, not the dollars.

items.q: Count by 10s. How much money is this?
items.e: Each $10 bill is $10. Count by 10s: $10, $20, $30. That is $30. $3 counts the pieces, not the dollars.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: $10, $15. That is $15. $2 counts the pieces, not the dollars.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: $20, $25. That is $25. $2 counts the pieces, not the dollars.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each $20 bill is $20. Count by 20s: $20, $40. That is $40. $2 counts the pieces, not the dollars.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the biggest one. Count on: $20, $30, $35. That is $35. $3 counts the pieces, not the dollars.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each loonie is $1. Count by 1s: $1, $2, $3, $4. That is $4. 4¢ thinks a loonie is 1¢.

items.q: Count by 2s. How much money is this?
items.e: Each toonie is $2. Count by 2s: $2, $4, $6. That is $6. A toonie is $2, not $1.

items.q: Who has more money?
items.e: Nathan has $20, $40. Lucas has $50. $50 is more, so Lucas has more. 2 bills is not always more money.

items.q: Who has more money?
items.e: Aiden has $10, $20. Benjamin has $5, $10, $15. $20 is more, so Aiden has more.

items.q: Who has more money?
items.e: Noah has 10¢, 20¢. Zoe has 5¢, 10¢, 15¢. 20¢ is more, so Noah has more. More coins is not always more money.

items.q: Who has more money?
items.e: Mei has $10. Leah has $5, $10. They have the same: $10 each.

items.q: At the bake sale, a cookie costs 25¢. Kai pays with 1 coin. Which coin pays exactly?
items.e: A quarter is 25¢, the same as the cookie.

items.q: Olivia had 2 dimes. She found 1 more dime. How much does she have now?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢. Olivia has 30¢. A dime is 10¢, not 1¢, so 21¢ is wrong.

items.q: Jayden puts 6 nickels in his piggy bank. How much is in it?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢. That is 30¢. 60¢ counts nickels by 10s.

items.q: Ethan has 4 dimes. He gives 1 dime to his sister. How much is left?
items.e: Ethan has 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢. Take away 1 dime: 40¢ − 10¢ = 30¢. 50¢ adds a dime instead.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Arjun gives this money. How much does he give?
items.e: $20, then count on 10: $30. Arjun gives $30. $2 counts the bills, not the dollars.

items.q: Hot chocolate at the rink costs $3. Liam has these coins. Does he have enough?
items.e: Toonie $2, loonie $1: $2, $3. Liam has $3, so yes. $2 comes from counting the toonie as $1.

items.q: A book costs $20. Maya has this money. Does she have enough?
items.e: $10, then count on 5: $15. $15 is less than $20, so no. $2 counts the bills, not the dollars.

items.q: Owen has 50¢ in dimes. How many dimes is that?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢, 50¢. That is 5 dimes. 10 would be nickels.
